name: Evidence Extraction Tables
title: Evidence Extraction Tables
answer: Evidence extraction tables are the structured grids in which a systematic review records what each included study reported, one row per study and one column per item of interest. They sit between the screening stage and the synthesis stage, and they hold the population, intervention, comparator, outcome, effect size, and risk of bias entries that later feed a meta analysis or a narrative summary. In a review of machine learning in medicine, for example, a table might capture model type, training data, validation method, and reported performance for every paper that passed screening.

sections.body: Evidence extraction tables are the structured grids in which a systematic review records what each included study reported, one row per study and one column per item of interest. They sit between the screening stage and the synthesis stage, and they hold the population, intervention, comparator, outcome, effect size, and risk of bias entries that later feed a meta analysis or a narrative summary. In a review of machine learning in medicine, for example, a table might capture model type, training data, validation method, and reported performance for every paper that passed screening.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on reference managers, spreadsheet software, and dedicated systematic review platforms, with PDFs of the included papers stored alongside the extraction sheet. Review teams often use a shared workbook or a hosted tool so that two extractors can work on the same table and a third can resolve disagreements. Version control matters more than it first appears, because a table that changes after the analysis has begun can invalidate the numbers already computed.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Extraction usually proceeds from a piloted form, tested on a handful of studies and revised before the full set is tackled. Two reviewers extract independently and then compare entries, with a third reviewer or consensus discussion settling conflicts. Each cell should trace to a page, table, or figure in the source paper, and where a study reports an outcome in an unusable form, the extractor records that gap rather than estimating a value. Automation can pre fill candidate fields from PDFs, but a human still verifies every entry against the original text.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The table is a provenance record as much as a data structure, so it should note who extracted each entry, when, and from which version of the paper. Copyright and licence terms govern how much of a source can be quoted or reproduced, and a table that copies large passages or whole figures may exceed fair dealing. Review protocols, registration entries, and data availability statements set expectations about what will be published, and discrepancies between the protocol and the final table need to be disclosed rather than quietly absorbed.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Extraction is moving toward semi automated pipelines in which language models propose candidate values and reviewers confirm or correct them, which shifts effort from typing to verification. Standards for reporting extraction decisions and for sharing tables as structured data are maturing, and journals increasingly expect the underlying table to accompany the review. The open question is how much of the judgement in extraction can be delegated without losing the audit trail that makes a review trustworthy.
